sentences.text: The bone originally thought to be a squamosal in the Monoclonius fissus specimen was actually a pterygoid.
The genus appears in the Advanced Dungeons & Dragons Monster Manual, featuring in both the first and second editions of the game.

The genus Monoclonius was first named by Edward Drinker Cope in 1876. This was the third ceratopsian genus he described, following Agathaumas and Polyonax. The type species, Monoclonius crassus, was also named by Cope in that same year. However, this specific species is currently considered a nomen dubium.
Lawrence Lambe later described three new species of Monoclonius from Canada in 1902 based on fragmentary skulls.
One of these, Monoclonius belli, named by Lambe in 1902, is now classified as Chasmosaurus belli.
The type and only specimen of Monoclonius lowei, cataloged as CMN 8790, was recovered from the upper strata of the Dinosaur Park Formation in Alberta.

Monoclonius is classified in the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Sauropsida, superorder Dinosauria, order Ornithischia, suborder Neornithischia, infraorder Ceratopsia, family Ceratopsidae, and subfamily Centrosaurinae.

It is debated whether the original type material of Monoclonius crassus belongs to a centrosaurine or a hadrosaurian, with some evidence suggesting it might be a hadrosaurian mistakenly associated with other fossils. In 1998, Peter Dodson and Allison Tumarkin argued that the bone structure of Monoclonius specimens could be explained by species-specific pedomorphosis, where adults retain juvenile traits. During the 1990s, the relationship between Monoclonius and Centrosaurus remained a subject of debate.
